    89	    # 'Ms. Karley Kiehn V'
    90	
    91	Pytest fixtures
    92	---------------
    93	
    94	``Faker`` also has its own ``pytest`` plugin which provides a ``faker`` fixture you can use in your
    95	tests. Please check out the `pytest fixture docs` to learn more.
    96	
    97	Providers
    98	---------
    99	
   100	Each of the generator properties (like ``name``, ``address``, and
   101	``lorem``) are called "fake". A faker generator has many of them,
   102	packaged in "providers".
   103	
   104	.. code:: python
   105	
   106	    from faker import Faker
   107	    from faker.providers import internet
   108	
   109	    fake = Faker()
   110	    fake.add_provider(internet)
   111	
   112	    print(fake.ipv4_private())
   113	
   114	
   115	Check the `extended docs`_ for a list of `bundled providers`_ and a list of
   116	`community providers`_.
   117	
   118	Localization
   119	------------
   120	
   121	``faker.Faker`` can take a locale as an argument, to return localized
   122	data. If no localized provider is found, the factory falls back to the
   123	default LCID string for US english, ie: ``en_US``.
   124	
   125	.. code:: python
   126	
   127	    from faker import Faker
   128	    fake = Faker('it_IT')
   129	    for _ in range(10):
   130	        print(fake.name())
   131	
   132	    # 'Elda Palumbo'
   133	    # 'Pacifico Giordano'
   134	    # 'Sig. Avide Guerra'
   135	    # 'Yago Amato'
   136	    # 'Eustachio Messina'
   137	    # 'Dott. Violante Lombardo'
   138	    # 'Sig. Alighieri Monti'
   139	    # 'Costanzo Costa'
   140	    # 'Nazzareno Barbieri'
   141	    # 'Max Coppola'
   142	
   143	``faker.Faker`` also supports multiple locales. New in v3.0.0.
   144	
   145	.. code:: python
   146	
   147	    from faker import Faker
   148	    fake = Faker(['it_IT', 'en_US', 'ja_JP'])
   149	    for _ in range(10):
   150	        print(fake.name())
   151	
   152	    # 鈴木 陽一
   153	    # Leslie Moreno
   154	    # Emma Williams
   155	    # 渡辺 裕美子
   156	    # Marcantonio Galuppi
   157	    # Martha Davis
   158	    # Kristen Turner
   159	    # 中津川 春香
   160	    # Ashley Castillo
   161	    # 山田 桃子
   162	
   163	You can check available Faker locales in the source code, under the
   164	providers package. The localization of Faker is an ongoing process, for
   165	which we need your help. Please don't hesitate to create a localized
   166	provider for your own locale and submit a Pull Request (PR).
   167	
   168	Optimizations
   169	-------------
   170	The Faker constructor takes a performance-related argument called
   171	``use_weighting``. It specifies whether to attempt to have the frequency
   172	of values match real-world frequencies (e.g. the English name Gary would
   173	be much more frequent than the name Lorimer). If ``use_weighting`` is ``False``,
   174	then all items have an equal chance of being selected, and the selection
   175	process is much faster. The default is ``True``.
   176	
   177	Command line usage
   178	------------------
   179	
   180	When installed, you can invoke faker from the command-line:
   181	
   182	.. code:: console
   183	
   184	    faker [-h] [--version] [-o output]
   185	          [-l {bg_BG,cs_CZ,...,zh_CN,zh_TW}]
   186	          [-r REPEAT] [-s SEP]
   187	          [-i {package.containing.custom_provider otherpkg.containing.custom_provider}]
   188	          [fake] [fake argument [fake argument ...]]
   189	
   190	Where:
   191	
   192	-  ``faker``: is the script when installed in your environment, in
   193	   development you could use ``python -m faker`` instead
   194	
   195	-  ``-h``, ``--help``: shows a help message
   196	
   197	-  ``--version``: shows the program's version number
   198	
   199	-  ``-o FILENAME``: redirects the output to the specified filename
   200	
   201	-  ``-l {bg_BG,cs_CZ,...,zh_CN,zh_TW}``: allows use of a localized
   202	   provider
   203	
   204	-  ``-r REPEAT``: will generate a specified number of outputs
   205	
   206	-  ``-s SEP``: will generate the specified separator after each
   207	   generated output
   208	
   209	-  ``-i {my.custom_provider other.custom_provider}`` list of additional custom
   210	   providers to use. Note that is the import path of the package containing
   211	   your Provider class, not the custom Provider class itself.
   212	
   213	-  ``fake``: is the name of the fake to generate an output for, such as
   214	   ``name``, ``address``, or ``text``
   215	
   216	-  ``[fake argument ...]``: optional arguments to pass to the fake (e.g. the
   217	   profile fake takes an optional list of comma separated field names as the
   218	   first argument)
   219	
   220	Examples:
   221	
   222	.. code:: console
   223	
   224	    $ faker address
   225	    968 Bahringer Garden Apt. 722
   226	    Kristinaland, NJ 09890
   227	
   228	    $ faker -l de_DE address
   229	    Samira-Niemeier-Allee 56
   230	    94812 Biedenkopf
   231	
   232	    $ faker profile ssn,birthdate
   233	    {'ssn': '628-10-1085', 'birthdate': '2008-03-29'}
   234	
   235	    $ faker -r=3 -s=";" name
   236	    Willam Kertzmann;
   237	    Josiah Maggio;
   238	    Gayla Schmitt;
   239	
   240	How to create a Provider
   241	------------------------
   242	
   243	.. code:: python
   244	
   245	    from faker import Faker
   246	    fake = Faker()
   247	
   248	    # first, import a similar Provider or use the default one
   249	    from faker.providers import BaseProvider
   250	
   251	    # create new provider class
   252	    class MyProvider(BaseProvider):
   253	        def foo(self) -> str:
   254	            return 'bar'
   255	
   256	    # then add new provider to faker instance
   257	    fake.add_provider(MyProvider)
   258	
   259	    # now you can use:
   260	    fake.foo()
   261	    # 'bar'
   262	
   263	
   264	How to create a Dynamic Provider
   265	--------------------------------
   266	
   267	Dynamic providers can read elements from an external source.
   268	
   269	.. code:: python
   270	
   271	    from faker import Faker
   272	    from faker.providers import DynamicProvider
   273	
   274	    medical_professions_provider = DynamicProvider(
   275	         provider_name="medical_profession",
   276	         elements=["dr.", "doctor", "nurse", "surgeon", "clerk"],
   277	    )
   278	
   279	    fake = Faker()
   280	
   281	    # then add new provider to faker instance
   282	    fake.add_provider(medical_professions_provider)
   283	
   284	    # now you can use:
   285	    fake.medical_profession()
   286	    # 'dr.'
   287	
   288	How to customize the Lorem Provider
   289	-----------------------------------
   290	
   291	You can provide your own sets of words if you don't want to use the
   292	default lorem ipsum one. The following example shows how to do it with a list of words picked from `cakeipsum <http://www.cupcakeipsum.com/>`__ :
   293	
   294	.. code:: python
   295	
   296	    from faker import Faker
   297	    fake = Faker()
   298	
   299	    my_word_list = [
   300	    'danish','cheesecake','sugar',
   301	    'Lollipop','wafer','Gummies',
   302	    'sesame','Jelly','beans',
   303	    'pie','bar','Ice','oat' ]
   304	
   305	    fake.sentence()
   306	    # 'Expedita at beatae voluptatibus nulla omnis.'
   307	
   308	    fake.sentence(ext_word_list=my_word_list)
   309	    # 'Oat beans oat Lollipop bar cheesecake.'
   310	
   311	
   312	How to use with Factory Boy
   313	---------------------------
   314	
   315	`Factory Boy` already ships with integration with ``Faker``. Simply use the
   316	``factory.Faker`` method of ``factory_boy``:
   317	
   318	.. code:: python
   319	
   320	    import factory
   321	    from myapp.models import Book
   322	
   323	    class BookFactory(factory.Factory):
   324	        class Meta:
   325	            model = Book
   326	
   327	        title = factory.Faker('sentence', nb_words=4)
   328	        author_name = factory.Faker('name')
   329	
   330	Accessing the `random` instance
   331	-------------------------------
   332	
   333	The ``.random`` property on the generator returns the instance of
   334	``random.Random`` used to generate the values:
   335	
   336	.. code:: python
   337	
   338	    from faker import Faker
   339	    fake = Faker()
   340	    fake.random
   341	    fake.random.getstate()
   342	
   343	By default all generators share the same instance of ``random.Random``, which
   344	can be accessed with ``from faker.generator import random``. Using this may
   345	be useful for plugins that want to affect all faker instances.
   346	
   347	Unique values
   348	-------------
   349	
   350	Through use of the ``.unique`` property on the generator, you can guarantee
   351	that any generated values are unique for this specific instance.
   352	
   353	.. code:: python
   354	
   355	   from faker import Faker
   356	   fake = Faker()
   357	   names = [fake.unique.first_name() for i in range(500)]
   358	   assert len(set(names)) == len(names)
   359	
   360	Calling ``fake.unique.clear()`` clears the already seen values.
   361	Note, to avoid infinite loops, after a number of attempts to find a unique
   362	value, Faker will throw a ``UniquenessException``. Beware of the `birthday
   363	paradox <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birthday_problem>`_, collisions
   364	are more likely than you'd think.
   365	
   366	
   367	.. code:: python
   368	
   369	   from faker import Faker
   370	
   371	   fake = Faker()
   372	   for i in range(3):
   373	        # Raises a UniquenessException

   377	with ``.unique``.

   387	.. code:: python

   392	
   393	    print(fake.name())

   396	Each generator can also be switched to its own instance of ``random.Random``,
   397	separate to the shared one, by using the ``seed_instance()`` method, which acts
   398	the same way. For example:
   399	
   400	.. code:: python
   401	
   402	    from faker import Faker
   403	    fake = Faker()
   404	    fake.seed_instance(4321)
   405	
   406	    print(fake.name())
   407	    # 'Margaret Boehm'

This tool provides structured task management capabilities for development workflows.
It enables systematic tracking of work items, progress monitoring, and efficient
organization of complex development activities.

The tool maintains visibility into project status and helps communicate
progress effectively to users.

## Application Guidelines

Utilize this tool in the following situations:

1. Multi-phase development work - When projects involve multiple sequential or
   parallel activities
2. Complex implementation tasks - Work requiring systematic planning and
   coordination across multiple components
3. Explicit user request for task organization - When users specifically ask
   for structured task management
4. Multiple concurrent requirements - When users present several work items
   that need coordination
5. Project initiation - Capture and organize user requirements at project start
6. Work commencement - Update task status to in_progress before beginning
   implementation. Maintain focus by limiting active work to one task
7. Task completion - Update status to done and identify any additional work
   that emerged during implementation

## Situations Where Tool Usage Is Unnecessary

Avoid using this tool when:

1. Single atomic tasks that require no decomposition
2. Trivial operations where tracking adds no organizational value
3. Simple activities completable in minimal steps
4. Pure information exchange or discussion

Note: For single straightforward tasks, proceed with direct implementation
rather than creating tracking overhead.

## Usage Scenarios

**Scenario A: Feature Development with Validation**
User request: "Build a user authentication system with login/logout functionality.
Don't forget to include input validation and error handling!"

Response approach: I'll implement a user authentication system with comprehensive
validation. Let me organize this work systematically.

*Task breakdown includes:*
1. Design authentication API endpoints and data models
2. Implement user login/logout controllers with session management
3. Add client-side form validation and error display
4. Create backend input sanitization and security checks
5. Implement comprehensive error handling for edge cases
6. Perform integration testing and fix any issues

**Scenario B: Codebase Refactoring**
User request: "I need to update all instances of the method 'fetchData' to
'retrieveInformation' throughout the entire project"

Response approach: Let me first analyze your codebase to identify all locations
where 'fetchData' appears.

*After code analysis*

I've located 12 occurrences of 'fetchData' across 6 files in your project.

*Organized task list includes specific file-by-file updates*

**Scenario C: Multi-feature Development**
User request: "Set up a blog platform with these components: admin dashboard,
article management, comment system, and user profiles."

Response approach: I'll help build your blog platform. Let me break down these
components into manageable implementation phases.

for (let i = 0; i < array.length; i++) {

1. **Status Values**: Track work using these states:
   - todo: Not yet initiated
